spans.title: How Dare I
spans.blurb: Trembling but unstoppable, a small girl finally tells the woman who raised her exactly what her coldness and cruelty have cost, and what she will tell the world.

spans.title: Thirty Miles to Land
spans.blurb: A storm-driven balloon sinks toward furious waves with land in sight; its passengers cling to the net and count the miles as the gas runs out.

spans.title: Mr. Collins's Proposal
spans.blurb: A pompous clergyman proposes marriage with his reasons numbered and his patroness quoted; the lady refuses plainly, but refusal is not an answer he recognizes.
spans.brokenNote: The text cuts off mid-sentence on a dangling comma in Mr. Collins's final reply.

spans.title: England Can Afford It
spans.blurb: A catastrophe has left thirteen soldiers on a shrunken island where days last six hours; the two officers in charge calmly finish their chess move and settle the men's pay.
spans.spoilerNote: It sketches the strange physical changes to the world whose cause the full book stages as a slow-dawning mystery.

spans.title: A Glance Between Strangers
spans.blurb: Stepping aside at a carriage door, an officer glances at a lady and must look again; something in her face keeps escaping her control.

spans.title: The Steeplechase
spans.blurb: Before the Tsar and all the crowd, an officer and his beloved mare fly the barriers together, a rival's hoofbeats never fading behind them.

spans.title: Twenty Minutes to Nine
spans.blurb: A boy is sent to play in a candlelit house where daylight never enters, before a lady in a yellowed bridal dress whose clocks stopped long ago.

spans.title: Taken with a Maid
spans.blurb: Arrested for being caught with a girl, a country clown disputes every word of the royal proclamation, from wench to damsel to maid.

spans.title: Four Woodcocks in a Dish
spans.blurb: A lord who swore an oath against love hides to watch his king and two friends, one by one, read aloud the sonnets they should never have written.

spans.title: Two Blushing Pilgrims
spans.blurb: At a masked feast, a stranger takes a girl's hand and turns one touch into a playful theology of saints and pilgrims; then he learns whose daughter she is.

spans.title: The Balcony Scene
spans.blurb: From a dark orchard, a young man overhears the girl he loves asking the night why a name should stand between them, and steps out to answer.

books.pairNote: Consecutive beats of one courtship, but the ball's banter and the balcony's vows each land on their own.

spans.title: The Sharp Athenian Law
spans.blurb: A father hauls his daughter before the duke, demanding an old law: wed the suitor he chose or die. Left alone, the lovers make another plan.
spans.brokenNote: Cuts off mid-sentence in Hermia's closing vow ('Tomorrow truly will'), leaving the ending hanging in the air.

spans.title: Hercules Be Thy Speed
spans.blurb: An unknown young man insists on wrestling the duke's fearsome champion while two ladies cheer him on; his father's name matters more than anyone expects.

spans.title: A Cure for Love
spans.blurb: Deep in the forest, a quick-tongued youth corners the poet who hangs love rhymes on trees and prescribes a strange cure: woo me as your Rosalind.
